beijing.blurb: Capital of the Qing emperors, whose Manchu banner garrisons guarded the gates of the Inner City. Opera troupes from Anhui, invited to court since 1790, were laying the foundations of what would become Peking Opera.

image.file: File:Plan of Peking in 1817.png
image.caption: Plan of Peking within its walls as it was in 1817, published in 1842.

london.polity: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
london.blurb: In 1825 Marc Brunel began the Thames Tunnel between Rotherhithe and Wapping, dug with his new tunnelling shield to link the docks on both banks. It became the first tunnel successfully built under a navigable river.

image.file: File:Thames Tunnel,1827, Museum of history and Technology.png
image.caption: Print of Brunel's Thames Tunnel project, 1827.

guangzhou.blurb: The only Chinese port open to most Western traders, who were confined to the Thirteen Factories along the Pearl River. Under this Canton System, exports of tea and porcelain made it one of the world's greatest ports.

image.file: File:Foreign factories, Canton.jpg
image.caption: The foreign factories on the Pearl River at Canton, painted between 1825 and 1835.

paris.blurb: Charles X succeeded his brother Louis XVIII in 1824, and the restored Bourbons were building neoclassical churches to replace those lost in the Revolution. The Canal Saint-Martin, bringing fresh water from the Ourcq, was completed in 1825.

image.file: File:Bassin de la Villette 1820.jpg
image.caption: The Barrière Saint-Martin and the basin of the Ourcq canal, coloured etching, about 1820.

tokyo.blurb: Seat of the Tokugawa shoguns, while the emperor remained in Kyoto. Its book trade was booming, with more than 800 booksellers by the 1830s, and artists such as Hokusai and Hiroshige were depicting its streets.

image.file: File:冨嶽三十六景 江戸日本橋-Nihonbashi in Edo (Edo Nihonbashi), from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei) MET DP141003.jpg
image.caption: Hokusai's woodblock print of Nihonbashi in Edo, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, about 1830-32.

1850.note: Industrialisation was drawing huge numbers of rural migrants into cities, first in Europe. London's population had more than doubled since 1800, making it by far the world's largest city.

london.polity: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
london.blurb: King's Cross, the latest of the great railway termini, opened in 1850. The next year the Great Exhibition in Hyde Park's Crystal Palace drew six million visitors and displayed Britain at the height of its imperial dominance.

image.file: File:Crystal Palace from the northeast from Dickinson's Comprehensive Pictures of the Great Exhibition of 1851. 1854.jpg
image.caption: The Crystal Palace in Hyde Park during the Great Exhibition of 1851, from Dickinson's Comprehensive Pictures (1854).

beijing.blurb: The 19-year-old Xianfeng Emperor took the throne in 1850, inheriting an empire in crisis. That December the Taiping Rebellion broke out in the south, and the Nian rebels' cavalry would soon threaten the capital itself.

image.file: File:Felice Beato (British, born Italy - Top of the Wall of Peking - Google Art Project.jpg
image.caption: Felice Beato's photograph from the top of Peking's city wall, October 1860, among the earliest photographs of the city.

paris.blurb: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte, elected president in 1848, ruled a crowded, unhealthy city where cholera had killed twenty thousand that year. He seized power in 1851, and his rebuilding of Paris with Haussmann began in 1853.

image.file: File:Charles Marville, Rue Tirechape, de la rue de Rivoli, ca. 1853–70, edited.jpg
image.caption: Charles Marville's photograph of the narrow Rue Tirechape in old central Paris, taken between about 1853 and 1870.

guangzhou.blurb: The 1842 Treaty of Nanking ended the Canton System, and trade was shifting to new treaty ports. The foreign factories, burned in the First Opium War, had been rebuilt, while local viceroys resisted opening the walled city to foreigners.

image.file: File:Canton c1850.jpg
image.caption: Gouache of the hongs, the foreign factories on the Pearl River at Canton, about 1850.

istanbul.blurb: Capital of the Ottoman Empire in the era of the Tanzimat reforms, which brought new technology and bridges across the Golden Horn. Sultan Abdülmecid I was building the European-style Dolmabahçe Palace on the Bosphorus to replace medieval Topkapı.

image.file: File:Robertson & Beato - Dolmabahçe Palace and Mosque - Google Art Project.jpg
image.caption: Dolmabahçe Palace and Mosque on the Bosphorus, photographed by Robertson & Beato in the mid-19th century.

london.polity: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
london.blurb: Joseph Bazalgette's vast sewer network, begun after the Great Stink of 1858, was cleaning up the Thames. The Underground, open since 1863, and new metropolitan railways let middle-class Londoners commute from spreading suburbs.

image.file: File:YCBA London a Pilgrimage 06 (cropped).jpg
image.caption: Gustave Doré's engraving 'Over London - by Rail', from London: A Pilgrimage (1872).

paris.blurb: Recovering from the 1871 Commune, whose fighters burned the Tuileries Palace and the Hôtel de Ville. The Palais Garnier opera house, begun under Napoleon III, was completed in 1875, and the Hôtel de Ville was being rebuilt.

image.file: File:Inauguration of the Paris Opera in 1875 by Detaille - Collections of the Château of Versailles (cropped).jpg
image.caption: Édouard Detaille's gouache of the inauguration of the Paris Opera on 5 January 1875, painted in 1878.

new-york.blurb: Its harbour handled most American exports, and Boss Tweed had been convicted in 1873 of defrauding the city. Across the East River, the Brooklyn Bridge's towers were rising to link Manhattan with the separate city of Brooklyn.

sources.title: History of New York City (1855–1897) - Wikipedia
History of New York City (1855–1897) - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Brooklyn Bridge tower in construction, from Robert N. Dennis collection of stereoscopic views.jpg
image.caption: Stereoscopic view of a Brooklyn Bridge tower under construction; the towers were built between 1872 and 1876.

berlin.blurb: Capital of the new German Empire since 1871, with its bureaucracy and military expanding fast. Sanitation was among the worst in Europe, and a modern sewer system was built in the late 1870s.

image.file: File:Kaisergalerie, Berlin 1875.jpg
image.caption: The Kaisergalerie shopping arcade on Friedrichstraße, opened in 1873, photographed around 1875.

vienna.blurb: The Ringstraße, a grand boulevard lined with palaces, had replaced the old city walls. The 1873 World's Fair in the Prater marked Franz Joseph's 25 years as emperor, but a cholera outbreak and a stock-market crash kept visitors away.

image.file: File:Rotunde Weltausstellung 1873.jpg
image.caption: Main entrance of the Rotunde, the centrepiece of the 1873 Vienna World's Fair, photographed in 1873.

london.polity: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
london.blurb: At the height of its influence as capital of one of history's largest empires. The London County Council, created in 1888, governed the capital, and in 1900 its county was divided into 28 metropolitan boroughs.

image.file: File:Cheapside photochrom.jpg
image.caption: Photochrom print of busy Cheapside in the City of London, made between 1890 and 1900.

new-york.blurb: Consolidated in 1898 from Manhattan, Brooklyn, the Bronx, Queens and Staten Island. Its first subway line, opened in 1904, would help bind the five boroughs together, while early skyscrapers rose in Manhattan.

sources.title: History of New York City (1898–1945) - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Columbus Circle Subway construction.jpeg
image.caption: Columbus Circle dug up for construction of the New York City Subway, March 1900.

paris.blurb: The Exposition Universelle drew fifty million visitors and popularised Art Nouveau worldwide, and the first Métro line opened in time for it. The Grand Palais and Petit Palais were built for the fair.

image.file: File:Grand entrance, Exposition Universal, 1900, Paris, France.jpg
image.caption: The monumental main entrance of the 1900 Exposition Universelle, photographed in 1900.

berlin.blurb: An industrial city whose electrical-machinery industry had boomed since the 1880s. Work on the U-Bahn had begun in 1896, and tenement blocks were filling Kreuzberg, Prenzlauer Berg, Friedrichshain and Wedding.

image.file: File:Berlin - Potsdamer Platz - um 1900.jpg
image.caption: Potsdamer Platz, flanked by the Grand Hotel Belle Vue and the Palast Hotel, around 1900.

chicago.blurb: In 1900 the new Sanitary and Ship Canal reversed the Chicago River to carry sewage away from Lake Michigan. The nation's railroad hub had hosted the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, and most residents were immigrants or their children.

sources.title: Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Flickr - …trialsanderrors - State Street north from Madison Street, Chicago, Illinois, 1900.jpg
image.caption: State Street looking north from Madison Street, photochrom print copyrighted 1900.

1925.note: In the interwar years cars, electric lighting and radio became common in the richest countries, and the Roaring Twenties preceded the Great Depression. In the early 1920s New York overtook London as the world's most populous urban area.

new-york.blurb: Harlem, the political capital of Black America, was the heart of the Harlem Renaissance, home to writers such as Langston Hughes and Zora Neale Hurston. Skyscrapers were transforming the skyline as housing spread across Queens and outer Brooklyn.

sources.title: History of New York City (1898–1945) - Wikipedia
History of New York City (1898–1945) - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Guests at breakfast party for Langston Hughes hosted by Regina Anderson and Ethel Ray at 580 St. Nicholas Avenue, Harlem, May 1925.jpg
image.caption: Guests at a breakfast party for Langston Hughes at 580 St. Nicholas Avenue, Harlem, May 1925.

london.blurb: The British Empire Exhibition at Wembley, open in 1924 and 1925, aimed to strengthen imperial bonds and trade. Suburbs of semi-detached houses were spreading beyond the County of London into Middlesex, Essex, Hertfordshire, Kent and Surrey.

image.file: File:Postcard British Empire Exhibition 1924 25.jpg
image.caption: Postcard of Wembley Stadium at the British Empire Exhibition, 1924.

tokyo.blurb: Rebuilding after the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake and the fires that followed. Concrete buildings had survived best, spurring a shift to earthquake-proof construction, and the first underground railway outside Europe and the Americas would open in 1927.

image.file: File:Groundbreaking ceremony of Tokyo Underground Railway 1.jpg
image.caption: Groundbreaking ceremony for the Tokyo Underground Railway's Ueno-Asakusa line, today's Ginza Line, 27 September 1925.

paris.blurb: In les années folles, artists and writers from around the world gathered in Montparnasse cafés, and the 1925 International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts gave Art Deco its name. The old fortifications were being torn down.

sources.title: International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Paris-FR-75-Expo 1925 Arts décoratifs-vue esplanade des Invalides.jpg
image.caption: The 1925 International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts on the Esplanade des Invalides, July 1925.

berlin.blurb: Enlarged by the 1920 Greater Berlin Act and stabilised after the 1923 hyperinflation, it was continental Europe's largest industrial city. The Golden Twenties brought booming nightlife, the new S-Bahn and Tempelhof airport.

image.file: File:Potsdamer Platz, Berlin (Max Missmann, 1925).png
image.caption: Max Missmann's photograph of traffic on Potsdamer Platz, 1925.

1950.note: From 1950, sizes come from the UN's World Urbanization Prospects, which counts urban agglomerations: a city plus its surrounding built-up area, regardless of administrative boundaries. Earlier years use historians' estimates, so part of the jump reflects this change.

noteSources.title: Glossary of demographic terms - World Urbanization Prospects

new-york.blurb: With many great cities in ruins after the war, New York took on new global prominence. The United Nations headquarters was rising beside the East River, and abstract expressionism was making the city the centre of the art world.

sources.title: History of New York City (1946–1977) - Wikipedia
Headquarters of the United Nations - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Manhattan en het gebouw van de Verenigde Naties gezien vanaf de andere kant van de East River. RP-F-F02353.jpg
image.caption: Manhattan and the new United Nations headquarters seen from across the East River, February 1950.

tokyo.blurb: Still under American occupation, with General MacArthur's headquarters in Marunouchi. Governed since 1943 as the Tokyo Metropolis, the bomb-damaged city would use profits from the Korean War, which began in 1950, for rebuilding.

image.file: File:Aerial view of downtown Tokyo, Ginza district, in 1950.jpg
image.caption: US Navy aerial photograph of the Ginza district, with the Imperial Palace grounds behind, late 1949 or early 1950.

london.blurb: Rebuilding was slow after so much housing was destroyed in the war, and the authorities were turning to high-rise flats to ease the shortage. The 1951 Festival of Britain on the South Bank would mark a new mood of optimism.

image.file: File:Festival of Britain Exhibition, 1951 (geograph 4571066).jpg
image.caption: The Festival of Britain on the South Bank in July 1951, with the Dome of Discovery and the Skylon.

osaka.blurb: The UN figure covers the wider Keihanshin region, including Kyoto and Kobe. American B-29 raids in 1945 had devastated large parts of Osaka, and the rebuilding of its factories and trade was under way.

image.file: File:Street In Osaka Japan (5660956263).jpg
image.caption: Busy street near Osaka's central station, 26 April 1950.

paris.blurb: Bread rationing had ended only in 1948, and most apartments lacked their own bathroom. In 1950 the government began building HLM low-rent housing on the city's edges, while strikes and Communist-led protests kept politics turbulent.

image.file: File:Bus in Paris 1950.jpg
image.caption: A Renault TN platform bus on route 168 at the Porte de Clignancourt, 1950.
